title: How To Distribute Your AI Game
author: bingewavecinema
selftext:
I wrote a topic about [AI games primarily releasing on Itch](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1uhkhq7/why_are_ai_gamedevs_only_releasing_on_itch/). While that is one approach, I saw a lot of misconceptions.

A little about me before I go in on distribution; I'm a developer, not a game dev, of 20 years turned marketer, and I've helped indies achieve near $1 million in sales in their first year of release with marketing.

Let's break this down for those wanting to release their games and earn money.

**Steam**

* Pros: Steam has millions of users who are willing to PAY for games. If you are able to correctly leverage Steam's algorithm and events, that can easily turn into a $50k to $100k payday for you. But you have to put in the work; focus on play testing, wishlists, and audience development starting a year out from launch.
* Cons: There is a $100 fee just to register your game, they have lengthy review processes. Also, a lot of Steam is a black box when it comes to optimizing your game, making it hard to understand what is working and what is not.

[Glitch.fun](http://Glitch.fun)

* Pros: A lot of built-in marketing tools, including influencers where you actually can pay them based on the sales they make. It was designed with discoverability as a first-class priority, the platform has a superior wishlist system, will help with player growth, and has the most advanced toolset out of any of the platforms. Audience is AI friendly and also willing to pay.
* Cons: New platform, smaller audience. $10 fee that can be bypassed.

[Itch.io](http://Itch.io)

* Pros: Very easy to set up and distribute your game, and it's free to do so. Very customizable homepages and branding design for your game. Good for very low-risk tests.
* Cons: Tools are extremely limited in every aspect when compared to other platforms. Audience there is not really willing to pay for games.

# Misconceptions

This is for those that want to make money with their games.

1. **Play Test On Itch:** You're wasting your time here. If you want to make money, play test on Steam because those play tests drive wishlists, and wishlists convert to sales.
2. **Steam Users Won't Buy AI:** Not true. Yes, there is AI hate, but that is NOT everyone. There are people that just want a good game to play. Fastest-growing apps are AI apps.
3. **Release On Steam When You Want Customers:** False. There is about a year's worth (or more) of pre-launch items you should be doing on the platform you want to make money on, and focus on wishlists and play tests on platforms to convert into sales later.
